pr_body:
Annotate all functions to have full signature available in `SHOW FUNCTIONS`.

Fixes #99853 and part of #100621

All available functions are now correctly annotated with types, and an additional `isAggregation` column has been added to the returned table.

Few assumptions made for the annotations:
* all functions who accept text now have arguments of type `keyword|text`, unless they accepts enum strings in which case I've used the `keyword` type only.
* in the case described above, I've tried to annotate as argument description the possible values (see `date_extract`)
* I had to slightly tweak some description copy changing from commas to semi-colon as there's a bug in the CSV parser used in tests (thanks @luigidellaquila for debugging this) cc @abdonpijpelink 

There are few notable exceptions to the annotation completeness who I have not been able to fix, so I've partially annotated them:
* `coalesce`
* ~~`mv_sum`~~ updated with recent `main` commit.
* `round`
* `mv_dedupe`

I'll create a separate issue for them.

issue_context.title: [ES|QL] New `show aggs` command for stats supported functions
issue_context.body:
### Description

We currently have the `show functions` command who prints the current supported functions for the `EVAL` command.
It would be helpful to have also an equivalent `show aggs` for the `STATS` command and its relative signatures.
comments:
An alternative approach here can be to leverage the existing `show functions` command, and add a new `supported commands` column in the returned table result with the `eval`/`stats`/`where`.
This would also provide a coverage for `where` command functions, which otherwise might need yet another command option.

I've just noticed that since #99736 the `show functions` is returning also aggregation functions, but there's currently no column to identify whether a function aggregates or not.

> This would also provide a coverage for `where` command functions, which otherwise might need yet another command option.

As for this @luigidellaquila confirmed that any `eval` supported function should just work in a `where` command.

> I've just noticed that since https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/99736 the show functions is returning also aggregation functions,

Actually the behavior was the same before that change.
I think it would be useful to have one more column in the result (eg. boolean `aggregate` ) to distinguish the two types

review_comments: @luigidellaquila is this one ok with you?
I wonder if we can write a checkstyle rule that forces these to be alphabetical!
